description: Resolve a name or an identifier to an OpenAlex ID. ALWAYS use this before filtering by entity — names are ambiguous, IDs are not. A name returns up to 10 autocomplete matches with disambiguation hints. An identifier — OpenAlex ID, DOI, ORCID, ROR, PMID, or ISSN, bare or in URL form — resolves directly to the record it addresses instead of running a name search. Short names share the bare OpenAlex ID shape (keyword p53 reads as publisher ID P53), so a bare OpenAlex ID that resolves nothing is searched as a name next. Two identifiers can address more than one entity type: a ROR names an organization's institution, funder, and publisher records alike, so it returns each one that exists (institution first) unless entity_type picks one of those three; and a Crossref Funder Registry DOI (10.13039/…) resolves to the funder unless entity_type is works. A PMCID is recognized as well, bare or as a PubMed Central URL, but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead.

entity_type.description: Entity type to search. Omit for cross-entity search (useful when entity type is unknown). With an identifier `query` it narrows only an identifier that can address more than one type: a ROR to institutions, funders, or publishers (omit it to get every one of the three that exists), and a Funder Registry DOI (10.13039/…) to works instead of the funder. Every other identifier resolves as the type it belongs to, whatever this names — except under keywords, where a bare OpenAlex ID shape ("P53") is searched as a keyword name, since keyword IDs are slugs.

filters.description: Narrow autocomplete results with filters, in the openalex_search_entities filter syntax. Example: restrict to a specific country or publication year range. Country fields take ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes ({"country_code": "DE"} on institutions) and `language` takes ISO 639-1 codes ("en"); alpha-3, numeric, ISO 639-2, and English-name forms are converted — a multi-word name is one value, so "South Korea|Japan" ORs two countries — and a value that cannot be a country code is rejected. A multi-word value on a field matched as whole text (display_name, geo.city, geo.region, awards.funder_display_name) matches as one phrase ({"geo.city": "New York"} on institutions; a comma, as in "University of California, Berkeley", is part of it, and it cannot contain a double quote of its own), "!" and "|" included, but cannot be ANDed with "+" in the same field. A value mixing "|" with an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND — is rejected, since OpenAlex drops every "|" alternative that ANDs more than one value; put the AND in a second key instead. Requires entity_type — filter fields belong to one entity type, so a name search across every type takes none, and a name query passing filters without entity_type is rejected. Applies to name queries only — an identifier lookup returns the records it addresses regardless.

query.description: Name or partial name to resolve. Also accepts an identifier, bare or in URL form — OpenAlex ID ("W2741809807", "F4320332161", or an OpenAlex record-page or API URL such as "https://openalex.org/works/W2741809807"), DOI ("10.1038/nature12373", or a funder's Funder Registry DOI such as "10.13039/100000001"), ORCID ("0000-0002-1825-0097"), ROR ("https://ror.org/00hx57361"), PMID ("12345678" or "https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12345678"), ISSN ("1234-5678") — which resolves straight to the record it addresses, or for a ROR up to three (see entity_type), instead of running a name search. A bare OpenAlex ID that resolves nothing is then searched as a name — under entity_type when given, and not at all when filters come without entity_type — since short names share its shape ("P53" is a keyword); under entity_type keywords it is searched as a name from the start. A keyword URL ("https://openalex.org/keywords/groundwater") resolves the same way; a bare keyword slug reads as a name and runs a name search, which finds it too. A PMCID ("PMC1234567" or a PubMed Central URL) is recognized but OpenAlex indexes no PMCIDs, so it resolves nothing — pass the work's PMID or DOI instead.

name: openalex_resolve_name

budget.description: What this call cost against the OpenAlex daily budget and what is left of it. Read `remainingUsd` here to size the search or traversal this resolution feeds. Absent when OpenAlex omitted the accounting headers.

costUsd.description: USD this call spent. Autocomplete is priced at the floor — resolving a name before filtering costs far less than the failed searches an ambiguous name causes.

prepaidRemainingUsd.description: USD left in the prepaid balance — a separate pool OpenAlex draws on only after the daily allowance runs out, and which the daily reset does not refill. Add it to `remainingUsd` for the full spendable amount. Absent when the account holds no prepaid balance.

remainingUsd.description: USD left in today's OpenAlex budget after this call.

resetsInSeconds.description: Seconds until the daily budget refills (midnight UTC).

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `filters_without_entity_type`: A name `query` passed `filters` without `entity_type`. Filter fields belong to one entity type, and a name search across every type takes no filters. `rate_limited`: OpenAlex throttled the autocomplete request for exceeding its per-second ceiling (HTTP 429). `upstream_budget_exhausted`: The OpenAlex daily usage budget is spent (HTTP 429). `upstream_plan_required`: A filter is one OpenAlex serves only on a paid plan — created_date, updated_date, or a from_/to_ form of either (HTTP 429 "Plan upgrade required"). `upstream_timeout`: OpenAlex did not respond within the request deadline. `upstream_unavailable`: OpenAlex was unreachable or unusable — HTTP 503, a connection failure, or a body that was empty, HTML, or unparseable JSON. `upstream_unauthorized`: OpenAlex rejected the API key (HTTP 401). `upstream_forbidden`: OpenAlex denied access to autocomplete (HTTP 403). `id_dot_segment`: An identifier `query` holds a `.` or `..` path segment, written plainly or percent-encoded. `comma_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value contains a comma, which collides with the OpenAlex filter separator, on a field that takes no phrase. Free-text search filters (any `.search` key, such as display_name.search) and fields matched as whole text (display_name, awards.funder_display_name, awards.funder_award_id, geo.city, geo.region, raw_affiliation_strings, block_key, parsed_longest_name, biblio fields) are exempt: a comma there is sent quoted, as part of the phrase. `invalid_country_code`: A country filter (a key ending in country_code, country_codes, or countries) holds a segment that cannot be a country code, such as a misspelled name, an unassigned number, "unknown", or two codes joined by a space ("DE US"). `mixed_and_or_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value puts "|" (OR) beside an AND operator — a "+", or a space on a field where words mean AND (on a country field a space is always part of a country name, and inside a language name it is part of the name). OpenAlex splits the value on "|" first and drops every alternative that ANDs more than one value, so no single value can carry both. `quote_in_filter_value`: A `filters` value sent to OpenAlex double-quoted holds a double quote inside its outer pair — a value the server quotes (a multi-word value on a field matched as whole text, or a value holding a comma on such a field or on a free-text search filter), or one the caller wrapped in double quotes on any filter but a free-text search. `upstream_invalid_params`: OpenAlex rejected an invalid filter field name on the autocomplete query (HTTP 400). `upstream_invalid_id_value`: A `filters` entry expecting an entity ID received a value that is not an OpenAlex ID — usually a name (HTTP 400). `query_too_long`: OpenAlex autocomplete failed (HTTP 500) on a `query` longer than the 1,000 characters it accepts when entity_type is set. `upstream_invalid_params_other`: OpenAlex rejected the autocomplete request (HTTP 400) for a reason other than an invalid field name. `upstream_validation_failed`: OpenAlex rejected the autocomplete request as semantically invalid (HTTP 422). Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

notice.description: Guidance notice. Set when nothing matched (echoes the query, and the filters when a name search applied them, and suggests corrections), when a bare OpenAlex ID resolved nothing and the query was searched as a name instead (names both outcomes, or why the name search did not run or finish), when an identifier query was passed name-search parameters that do not apply to it, or when one of the lookups for a ROR failed upstream (names the entity type whose record may be missing). Absent otherwise.

results.description: Matches: up to 10 autocomplete matches for a name; for an identifier, the record it addresses — for a ROR, up to three, institution then funder then publisher — or none.

items.description: A single autocomplete match with its ID, name, entity type, activity stats, and a disambiguation hint.

cited_by_count.description: Citation count (direct for works, aggregate for others).

display_name.description: Human-readable name as plain text, with HTML entities decoded and markup removed. null only for an identifier lookup that landed on a record OpenAlex holds no title for (paratext works and other untitled entries) — use `id` to identify it.

entity_type.description: Entity type — one of: work, author, source, institution, topic, keyword, publisher, funder.

external_id.description: Canonical external ID (DOI, ORCID, ROR, ISSN).

hint.description: Disambiguation context as plain text — last institution (authors), host organization (sources), place or country (institutions); author names (works) from a name search, publication year from an identifier lookup. null when the record carries none.

works_count.description: Associated works. null for works themselves.
